rules.text: The inbox is JSONL: `<runs-root>/<run-id>/inbox.jsonl`, one object per line `{external_id, kind, title, description, payload, created_at}` with kind ∈ add/amend/split/merge/conflict/resolve/proposal.

Async command table: `--requirement 'title|description'` (add) / `--proposal 'rN|rev|stage|summary|artifacts[|changes]'` (proposal; the external_id is appended automatically as the 7th segment) / `--amend 'rN|new title|new description|deps'` (rev+1) / `--split 'rN|child A|child B'` / `--merge 'r2,r3|title|description'` / `--conflict 'r1,r2|note'` / `--resolve 'r1,r2|keep_both'`.
The async commands only append to the inbox (`OpenOptions::append`); they never read or write the autosave, so `--mod` is not needed and they may run concurrently with a live run.

Consumption points: before every automatic advancement under `cmd`, before every prompt under `stdin`, and before every single-shot dispatch — new lines are drained and dispatched by kind; a line that arrived while the run was live must never be missed.

The cross-process protocol is protocol-level mutual exclusion (not "read the file one more time"): `coordination.lock` in the run directory (create_new exclusion, a stale lock is taken over after 2s by mtime) plus `coordination.json` `{phase, writers, owner_pid, heartbeat_at}` with phase ∈ running / closing / finalized.

A write command registers first: phase=running → it counts as a writer until its line is on disk; phase=closing (heartbeat not expired) → the command itself fails non-zero (exit 3); phase=finalized → non-zero refusal (exit 3, a new run is required).

Before dispatching the final `review.note`, automatic advancement switches phase to closing, waits until the in-flight writers reach zero, and then does one last drain under the same protection: when a new requirement exists and is not done → lift closing and continue the loop (no ending); when nothing new arrived → finish `review.note` + settle under the same protection and set phase=finalized. So "the write command succeeded but the run already crossed the last drain" is impossible by protocol.

Stale lines and crash recovery: closing keeps itself alive with a heartbeat (expires after 10s); once expired, a write command or `--resume` declares it dead and returns the phase to running; the lock is taken over by mtime as well — neither can wedge forever after a process crash.

A standalone `--settle` also goes through closing: with unconsumed lines it returns `ok=false` and reverts to running (a resume can consume them); when already finalized it returns the old report idempotently and rewrites nothing.

The cursor (`{consumed:N}` in `inbox.cursor`) only advances after a dispatch succeeded and its save is on disk; replay relies on `external_id`: add / proposal → the Mod checks per-entity ext duplicates (`[REPLAY:REQ]` / `[REPLAY:PROPOSAL]`); amend / split / merge / conflict / resolve → a trailing `@ext=` on the payload plus `inbox.last` de-duplication (`[REPLAY:ASYNC]`).
A malformed line is skipped and the cursor advances past it (otherwise it would block forever).

Hard settlement gate: if `--settle` finds an unconsumed line it returns `ok=false` and a non-zero exit (it re-checks after writing: a line that arrives during settlement invalidates the report) — so "deliver after the ending" can never silently succeed; a new run is required.
Delivery after the process exited belongs to a new run: the inbox keeps the lines for the next run to consume, and settlement reports an error.
